title: HYPE randomized trial at Amsterdam UMC: the Hypotension Prediction Index with a treatment protocol cuts intraoperative hypotension
summary: In the HYPE trial at Amsterdam UMC, the Hypotension Prediction Index cut median time in hypotension during surgery from 32.7 to 8.0 minutes per patient.
account: Anesthesiologists at Amsterdam UMC (location AMC) in the Netherlands ran the HYPE randomized trial among adults having elective noncardiac surgery under general anesthesia with invasive blood pressure monitoring, enrolled from May 2018 to March 2019. In the intervention group, clinicians used the Hypotension Prediction Index, a machine learning early warning system from Edwards Lifesciences that predicts hypotension from the arterial waveform, together with a diagnostic and treatment protocol. Of 68 randomized patients, 60 completed the trial. The median time-weighted average of hypotension fell from 0.44 to 0.10 mm Hg, and median time in hypotension fell from 32.7 to 8.0 minutes per patient. The trial was small and ran at one center, and it measured a physiological outcome with no clinical outcome. Edwards Lifesciences funded the trial; the authors report that the company took no part in its design, analysis or reporting. In 2023, anesthesiologists at University Hospital Dubrava in Zagreb, Croatia, who received no outside funding, reported that the index also reduced the number and duration of hypotensive episodes in 34 patients having thoracic surgery.
purpose: The index was built to predict hypotension minutes before it happens so that clinicians can prevent it. Less hypotension was that purpose.
